affectedPublicSurfaces: NO HTTP route, no `/v1` surface, no UI, no vendor contract. Both subjects are Celery Beat tasks: `cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile_beat_tick` (registered `juli_backend.cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile`, `workers/tasks/cdp_batch_reconcile.py`) and `mock_analytics_hourly_reconcile` -> `run_mock_analytics_reconcile_orchestrated` (`workers/tasks/mock_analytics_reconcile.py`). Neither creates a `workflow_runs` row, which is exactly why W8-A's rollup (#1653) cannot make them visible. The only surface this slice changes is the structured JSON log stream: `configure_logging` installs one `_JuliManagedStreamHandler` with a `JsonFormatter` on the ROOT logger (`core/observability/logging.py`) and merges every non-standard `extra=` key at the top level of one JSON object per line, so a new field is readable by an operator query with no other change anywhere.

The two EVENT NAMES are the operator contract, and they are what a query keys on: `cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile_tick_complete` and `mock_analytics_reconcile_orchestrated_completed`. Renaming either, or replacing one with a differently-named event, breaks the one query this slice exists to make possible. Keep the names; change what they carry.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT, verified on this branch: the tick has TWO early returns and they are NOT equally silent. `if not _is_enabled(): return` (cdp_batch_reconcile.py lines 57-58) writes nothing at all - no log line of any kind. `if not enabled_shops:` (lines 61-66) ALREADY logs `cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile_skipped` with `extra={'reason': 'empty_allowlist'}`. The ~0.002s 'succeeded' 188 times on 2026-09-05 is the FLAG-OFF path, the one with no line at all. The empty-allowlist path is the weaker case, not an equal one. (Also verified: `_get_enabled_shops()` re-checks `_is_enabled()` itself, so the flag is consulted twice on the enabled path - pre-existing, not this slice's to change.)

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT, verified on this branch: `SharedComputeResult` (`services/cdp_speed/shared_compute_orchestrator.py:77-84`) carries `bronze_appended: int`, `silver_promoted: int`, `gold_written: bool`, `scoring_dispatched: bool`, `scoring_succeeded: bool | None`. `gold_written` is a BOOLEAN, not a count. Two of the three the issue calls 'the exact counts of work done' are counts; the third is a flag. The issue's own build instruction correctly names only `bronze_appended` and `silver_promoted` - follow the instruction, not the prose.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT, verified on this branch: the counts are not absent from the journal today. `SharedComputeOrchestrator.run` already emits `shared_compute_job_completed` carrying `bronze_appended`, `silver_promoted`, `gold_written`, `scoring_dispatched` and a `correlation_id` (`job_correlation_token(job.shop_id, job.idempotency_key)`). What is wrong is narrower and still worth fixing: the TASK's own completion line reports `fetch_plan_size` - the size of the REQUESTED plan - so the task line and the orchestrator line answer different questions and a reader of the task line alone cannot tell a zero cycle from a full one. State it that way in the PR; do not claim the counts were nowhere.

A TEST SEAM THAT WILL SILENTLY DEFEAT THIS SLICE: `run_mock_analytics_reconcile_orchestrated` takes `orchestrator_run_fn: Callable | None`, and on that branch it does `await orchestrator_run_fn(job)` and DISCARDS the return value. Every existing test that drives the task through that seam therefore proves nothing about the counts. If the seam stays, its contract changed (it must now return a `SharedComputeResult`) and the PR says so; at least one assertion must drive the REAL `run_shared_compute_job` path regardless.

Operator-visible effect, which is the whole point: `succeeded` with `enqueued_count = 0` becomes readable as a no-op rather than as work, and `succeeded` with `bronze_appended = 0, silver_promoted = 0` becomes distinguishable from `succeeded` with N - in one query over the JSON log stream, with no new table and no new surface.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO schema change of any kind. No new table, no new column, no Alembic revision, no backfill. Neither task writes a record row of its own today and this slice does not give either one: `TikTokSyncState` is written by `workers/services/polling`, not by either of these, and `workflow_runs` belongs to the agent stack which neither task enters. The only thing that changes is the content of two structured log lines. The Alembic tip on this branch is `058_juli_app_update_grants` (the issue text says 057, which was the tip when it was filed - 058 has since landed; recheck at implementation time and cite what is actually there). Stable and candidate are trivially compatible because no shared persisted state is involved. If implementation concludes it needs schema - it must not; a no-op-visibility fix that persists a row is the wrong design and was settled against by #1652 - this plan must be revised to schemaChangeInScope: true BEFORE merge, and the migration number must be RESERVED BY META: never computed from `alembic heads` and never read off the tip of the versions directory. W6 and W9-A hold unlanded numbers in flight, and this tree already carries two duplicate-number pairs (003 and 043) from exactly that mistake. As of this plan, this slice needs no migration number.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: the flag-off tick continues to return in ~2ms having written nothing, and the hourly reconcile continues to log `fetch_plan_size` while discarding the `SharedComputeResult` it already receives. That is not neutral - it is choosing the status quo in which 188 'successes' and 188 no-ops look identical. Nothing is partially applied, no schema moves, no data is at risk, and no new exposure is created by holding.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the previous release and restart juli-celery-worker and juli-celery-beat. Code-only and log-only: no schema state, no data effect, no vendor effect, nothing to reverse, and no migration to downgrade. Two honest caveats belong in the PR. First, a rollback RE-SILENCES the flag-off tick - lines already written stay written, but from the moment of the rollback the no-op is invisible again. Second, if any operator query or runbook has begun keying on `enqueued_count`/`bronze_appended`/`silver_promoted` by the time of a revert, that query returns nothing after the revert and must be reverted with it; do not describe the rollback as clean without saying so.

doNotInfer: Do NOT create a table, a column, a task-result row, or a `workflow_runs` row for either task. #1652 settled this and #1653's executor confirmed these two tasks are outside the rollup's reach. The record each task already emits is its structured JSON log line; this slice makes that line always fire and makes it honest about the count.

Do NOT log a count you do not have. A crash before `run_shared_compute_job` returns leaves the caller with NO `SharedComputeResult` - `SharedComputeOrchestrator.run` has no try/except around its three stages. Record the bronze count as explicitly unknown, or obtain the real partial count without changing the orchestrator's per-stage commit semantics. A hardcoded `0` on the crash path is forbidden by name: a defaulted zero is indistinguishable from a real no-op, which is the exact signal this slice exists to create.

Do NOT let the outer `try/finally` swallow the exception. The completion fact must be emitted AND the exception must still propagate. A task that crashes and reports a clean completion is a worse lie than a task that says nothing.

Do NOT rename `cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile_tick_complete` or `mock_analytics_reconcile_orchestrated_completed`, and do NOT introduce a third event name in their place. The event name is the operator's query key.
Do NOT drop `fetch_plan_size` from the mock-analytics completion line. It is the REQUESTED plan size; the new counts are what was WRITTEN. Two different questions, both worth answering.
Do NOT delete `cdp_batch_staggered_reconcile_skipped` silently. If it is folded into the completion line, say so in the PR - an existing line is an existing contract.
Do NOT treat `gold_written` as a count. It is a `bool` on `SharedComputeResult`. The issue's build instruction names only `bronze_appended` and `silver_promoted`; add those.

Do NOT modify `SharedComputeOrchestrator`, `run_shared_compute_job`, `_make_hourly_gap_fetch_plan`, the quota-guard filter, the idempotency key, or `BatchReconcileOrchestrator`. This slice captures a value that is already returned and emits a line that is already defined. If the crash-path count genuinely requires an orchestrator change, REPORT it rather than making it - the orchestrator's per-stage commit + `with_shop_scope` re-entry is load-bearing (#1576) and is shared by every material trigger, not just this task.

Do NOT change `configure_logging`, `JsonFormatter`, the one-JSON-object-per-line contract, the top-level `extra=` merge, or the handler-clearing rule. A new field rides the existing `extra={...}` surface and nothing else moves.

Do NOT derive any count by parsing a log line back out of the journal. Logs are for humans and incidents, never for arithmetic (PRD #1652). The counts come from `SharedComputeResult` and from the `enqueued_count` the loop already accumulates.

Do NOT assert by reading the module source, and do NOT assert a value that a test itself supplied without ever passing through the real code path. Every assertion reads the EMITTED log record. Bind every collaborator to the REAL object's signature - `celery_app.send_task`, `run_shared_compute_job` - never a `**kwargs` double, which proves routing and not that the real call would work.

Do NOT prove the mock-analytics counts through `orchestrator_run_fn` alone. That seam discards its return value today; a test that only drives it is a test of the test. At least one assertion goes through the real `run_shared_compute_job`.

Do NOT run the medallion-path assertions on SQLite. `SharedComputeOrchestrator.run` commits per stage and re-enters `with_shop_scope` around each one; a `SET LOCAL` GUC and a real COMMIT are Postgres behaviour. Use `tests/support/postgres.py` and bind the session factory to an ENGINE, not to a pre-opened connection - a session joining an already-active connection treats `commit()` as a SAVEPOINT release and no commit-related tenancy defect can be observed.
Do NOT put a production shop id in `CDP_BATCH_STAGGERED_RECONCILE_ALLOWLIST` on the candidate, and do NOT point the candidate's `DEMO_REFERENCE_SHOP_ID` at anything but the demo reference shop.
Do NOT widen into `workers/services/polling/` or `TikTokSyncState`. That is the integrations-domain carve-out named in the Architect brief; these two task modules are backend.
Do NOT touch apps/**, packages/**, ios/** - this epic's doNotLoad list - and do not open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051).

The migration number, if one ever proves necessary, is Meta-assigned. Never compute `down_revision` from head: W6 and W9-A hold unlanded numbers and this tree already carries duplicate 003 and 043 pairs from that mistake.
